name: Shin Hyun-seong
category: E-commerce / fintech founder (Ticket Monster, Terraform Labs co-founder)
milestone_by_age_26: In May 2010 at age 24, co-founded Ticket Monster (TMON), a South Korean Groupon-style mobile e-commerce company that scaled to tens of millions in monthly revenue within roughly a year and later sold to LivingSocial/Groupon.
early_history_summary: Born Shin Hyun-seung in Seoul on 12 November 1985 and known as Daniel Shin; moved to the Washington, D.C. area at age 9, attended Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology, and graduated Wharton (UPenn) in 2008. Co-founded Invite Media in college (raised ~$1M), worked at McKinsey, then returned to Korea and launched Ticket Monster in May 2010 with a tiny team and roughly $10,000.
primary_leverage_engine: Execution / operations on mobile commerce wave
family_context_summary: Korean family relocated to suburban Washington, D.C., when he was 9; parents emphasized elite U.S. education and prestige careers (e.g., McKinsey) over early startups.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents not documented as e-commerce or tech operators; pressure was toward consulting/finance legitimacy rather than domain apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Wharton, TJHSST, McKinsey, Groupon clone wave, Korea returnee founder, college startup reps
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and contemporaneous reporting (Phys.org/AFP May 2011; Inc. 2011) date Ticket Monster’s founding to May 2010 when Shin was 24–25 and document rapid scale from ~$10k and five people to major Korean social commerce player, with LivingSocial/Groupon acquisition paths reported. College Invite Media raise and McKinsey/Wharton background show prior reps and elite pipeline. Later co-founded Terraform Labs (with Do Kwon), Bass Ventures, and PortOne; Terra-related legal issues followed the 2022 collapse.
starting_point: Born in Seoul (12 Nov 1985); family moved to suburban Washington, D.C., at age 9; elite U.S. magnet high school and Wharton path with parental emphasis on prestigious careers.
current_position: Founder and co-CEO of fintech payment-orchestration company PortOne Global; founding partner at Bass Ventures; known as Ticket Monster founder and Terraform Labs co-founder (later indicted in South Korea related to Terra; has denied operational involvement after 2020).

trajectory.event: Co-founded Invite Media in college and later raised roughly $1 million in venture capital.
Co-founded Ticket Monster (TMON) in Seoul in May with a tiny team and about $10,000 in capital.
Scaled TMON rapidly; company later sold into LivingSocial/Groupon ownership path at a large multi-hundred-million valuation.
Co-founded Fast Track Asia company builder; became a flagship Korean returnee entrepreneur profiled nationally.
Co-founded Terraform Labs with Do Kwon, launching the Terra blockchain/stablecoin ecosystem.
Founded PortOne Global (payment orchestration; later CHAI-related ecosystem).
Indicted in South Korea on charges related to Terra collapse; denied operational control after 2020.

name: Owen Astrachan
milestone_by_age_26: Major recognition came with Duke faculty work from 1993 (~age 37), textbooks, NSF CISE Distinguished Education Fellow (2007), and ACM Outstanding Educator Award (2016); no specific dated material founder/research breakthrough by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born New York City 1956; Dartmouth AB mathematics 1978; Duke MAT 1979; taught high school math/CS 1980–85; Duke MS 1989 and PhD 1992; joined Duke faculty 1993 and later led AP Computer Science Principles development.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Duke bio place birth in 1956. By age 26 (1982) he was an early-career high-school teacher after Dartmouth/Duke MAT—not yet a published CS researcher or faculty leader. Signature milestones (Duke practice faculty, AP CSP PI, ACM Karlstrom) occur from mid-30s onward.

name: Marko Elez
milestone_by_age_26: Public notoriety arrived with DOGE/Treasury access controversies in 2025 at about age 25–26; SpaceX/X employment shows early technical hiring but no independently verified founding, product breakout, or field-defining milestone by age 26.
early_history_summary: Raised in Montgomery Township, NJ; Montgomery High School 2018; Rutgers CS (graduated early 2021). Full-time SpaceX software engineer from ~Oct 2020 (vehicle/Starship/Starlink software), later X and xAI; joined DOGE with high-visibility Treasury payment-system access and subsequent resignation/rehire controversy.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and FOIA resume material document young SpaceX engineering roles and DOGE work, but the project bar requires a material dated achievement (founding, seminal publication, major award). Employment at Musk companies and political controversy do not alone establish a qualifying success-by-26 milestone under conservative coding.

name: Kris Nova
milestone_by_age_26: Best-known Kubernetes maintainer work (kops, kubicorn, Heptio/VMware, GitHub Principal Engineer, Aurae/Nivenly) is documented mainly from the mid-2010s onward when she was already past 26; no specific dated material milestone at or before age 26 verified.
early_history_summary: Open-source engineer and alpinist known for Linux/Kubernetes contributions, kubicorn, CNCF advocacy, Hacking Kubernetes author, Nivenly Foundation co-founder, and GitHub Principal Engineer; died in a climbing accident 16 August 2023. Rest in Code memorial lists birth 4 November 1986 (CSV birth year 1990 appears incorrect).
evidence_summary: Memorial and industry obituaries place birth in 1986 and death in 2023. Kubernetes was open-sourced in 2014 (age ~27–28); major maintainer/advocate recognition and Principal Engineer role came later. Without a clearly dated pre-2013 breakout achievement, coded ineligible.

name: Jaime Carbonell
milestone_by_age_26: In 1979 at age 25–26, completed a Yale PhD under Roger Schank (thesis Subjective Understanding: Computer Models of Belief Systems) and joined Carnegie Mellon University as assistant professor of computer science, launching a top-tier AI/NLP academic career.
early_history_summary: Born 29 July 1953 in Montevideo, Uruguay; earned dual BS degrees in physics and mathematics from MIT in 1975; PhD in computer science at Yale under Roger Schank in 1979; immediately joined CMU CS faculty and later founded and directed the Language Technologies Institute, co-shaped early machine-learning conferences/books, and advanced machine translation and summarization research.
family_context_summary: Born in Montevideo, Uruguay; family background beyond nationality and later U.S. academic trajectory not detailed in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT BS, Yale PhD under Schank, CMU faculty at 26, early ML conference leadership
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and CMU memorials confirm birth 1953, MIT 1975, Yale PhD 1979 under Schank, and CMU hire in 1979—placing a dual elite-degree and top-AI-faculty launch at age 25–26. Later work (ML book series with Michalski/Mitchell, LTI founding, AAAI Fellow, Okawa Prize) built on that early appointment. Family domain advantages are not documented; institutional mentorship and selective pipelines are the clear early stack.
starting_point: Born 29 July 1953 in Montevideo, Uruguay; later U.S. elite STEM education at MIT and Yale; family financial/domain details not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died 28 February 2020 at age 66; final role Allen Newell Professor of Computer Science and founding director of CMU’s Language Technologies Institute.

trajectory.event: Earned dual BS degrees in physics and mathematics from MIT.
Completed Yale CS PhD under Roger Schank (Subjective Understanding) and joined CMU as assistant professor of computer science.
Co-edited early foundational Machine Learning volume with Michalski and Mitchell and helped organize the early ML conference series.
Appointed full professor at CMU.
Elected AAAI Fellow.
Named Allen Newell Chair; built LTI into a leading language-technologies institute.
Awarded the Okawa Prize for contributions to language technologies and AI.
Died 28 February 2020 after extended illness.

name: Eugene Yan
milestone_by_age_26: No reliable public birth year found; documented career milestones (Lazada ML lead, Amazon principal applied scientist, Anthropic MTS, eugeneyan.com writing) lack dated age-≤26 material achievements verifiable from two sources.
early_history_summary: Singapore-born applied scientist and writer known for recommendation systems and LLM engineering writing; psychology background (Singapore Management University), later ML roles at IBM/Lazada/healthtech and Amazon; as of 2026 Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic.
evidence_summary: Personal site and Amazon Science profile document a strong applied-ML career and public technical writing, but without a confirmed birth year and without a specific independently dated breakthrough at ≤26, eligibility cannot be established under strict rules.

name: Tom Occhino
milestone_by_age_26: No reliable public birth year found; known for joining Facebook ~2009 and later leading React platform work and keynotes (React Conf), then CPO at Vercel—milestones not datable to age ≤26 without age evidence.
early_history_summary: Former Facebook engineering director associated with React’s growth and open-source keynotes; later Chief Product Officer at Vercel leading engineering, product, and design; SUNY Buffalo education noted on LinkedIn.
evidence_summary: Public profiles confirm React/Facebook leadership and Vercel CPO role, but sources do not establish birth year or any specific material milestone proven to have occurred at or before age 26.

name: Anne Wojcicki
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded 23andMe in 2006 at age 32–33; by age 26 (1999–2000) she was still early in post-Yale healthcare analyst work—no material founder milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Palo Alto 28 July 1973 to Stanford physics professor Stanley Wojcicki and educator Esther Wojcicki; Yale BS biology 1996; healthcare investment analyst for several years; co-founded 23andMe in 2006 with Linda Avey and Paul Cusenza; later public company CEO, bankruptcy/exit events in 2025, and TTAM buyback path.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and major profiles date birth 1973 and 23andMe founding to 2006 (age ~33). Age-26 window falls during Wall Street/healthcare analyst period after Yale, not company founding or product launch.

name: Victor Basili
milestone_by_age_26: PhD from University of Texas at Austin in 1970 at age ~30 and UMD faculty hire the same year; major Software Engineering Laboratory and Goal Question Metric contributions came later—no material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born 13 April 1940 (Brooklyn per Wikipedia); Fordham/Syracuse background then UT Austin PhD 1970; University of Maryland CS faculty from 1970, department chair 1982–88; pioneer of empirical software engineering and SEL at NASA/UMD; IEEE Fellow and multiple lifetime awards.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and UMD profiles place PhD and faculty start in 1970 when he was about 30. Age 26 was ~1966, during graduate studies before the documented career-defining academic appointment.

name: Kenyatta Cheese
category: Internet culture researcher / Know Your Meme co-founder
milestone_by_age_26: No public birth year found; College of New Jersey BA 1996 and Know Your Meme co-creation while at Rocketboom (~late 2000s) cannot be confirmed as age-≤26 milestones without age data.
early_history_summary: South Bronx–raised internet culture figure; TCNJ Communications Studies 1996; early video blogging, Rocketboom infrastructure work, co-created Know Your Meme with Jamie Wilkinson and Elspeth Rountree; later co-founded consultancy Everybody at Once (2013).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia documents education and Know Your Meme founding but omits birth year. If a typical ~22 graduation in 1996 is assumed, KYM would fall well after age 26; without verified birth year, coded ineligible.

name: Andy Baio
category: Web entrepreneur / technologist (Upcoming, Kickstarter CTO, XOXO)
milestone_by_age_26: In 2003 at age 26, launched Upcoming.org, a collaborative social event calendar that received New York Times coverage that year and was acquired by Yahoo for about $2 million in 2005.
early_history_summary: American technologist and blogger born 1977; ran the long-running Waxy.org blog from 2002 while working as a webmaster at a Texas financial company; founded Upcoming in 2003; later Yahoo technical director, Kickstarter board member and CTO, XOXO festival co-founder, and creator of projects including Skittish.
primary_leverage_engine: Product / domain insight + early web distribution
family_context_summary: Mother Toni Allen was a journalism professor and head of journalism at Oxnard College; other family financial details not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother’s journalism/media career provided adjacent media literacy; not a direct tech-startup apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Waxy.org linkblog, early social web, Upcoming product, web community distribution
evidence_summary: Wikipedia places birth in 1977 and Upcoming launch in 2003 (age ~26), with NYT Online Diary coverage (Nov 2003) and Yahoo acquisition (~$2M, 2005). Waxy.org blogging from 2002 built native distribution before the acquisition. Later Kickstarter CTO and XOXO co-founding extend the independent-web operator trajectory. Family evidence is limited to a journalism-professor mother.
starting_point: Born 1977 in the United States; mother Toni Allen was a journalism professor at Oxnard College; early career as a webmaster while building Waxy.org.
current_position: Portland-based technologist and Waxy.org author; co-founder of XOXO festival; former Kickstarter CTO; recent projects include Skittish (shut down 2022) and ongoing independent web work.

trajectory.event: Began long-running Waxy.org linkblog while working as a webmaster.
Launched Upcoming.org collaborative event calendar; covered by the New York Times Online Diary.
Yahoo acquired Upcoming for about $2 million; joined Yahoo as the site’s technical director.
Became Kickstarter CTO after earlier joining its board.
Co-founded the XOXO festival in Portland with Andy McMillan.
Launched Skittish virtual-events platform (later shut down in 2022).

name: Wendy Schmidt
milestone_by_age_26: Major public impact is philanthropic leadership from 2006 onward (Schmidt Family Foundation, Schmidt Ocean Institute, Schmidt Sciences) at age 50+; early Sun Microsystems marketing role (~employee #42 in 1982) falls at about age 26–27 but is not a material founder/research breakthrough by 26 under conservative coding.
early_history_summary: Born Wendy Susan Boyle 26 July 1955 in Orange, NJ; Smith College BA 1977; UC Berkeley journalism MA; marketing at Plexus then Sun Microsystems (employee #42, left after IPO 1986); later interior design firm; married Eric Schmidt 1980; large-scale climate/ocean/science philanthropy since 2006.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and foundation bios document birth 1955 and philanthropy from 2006. Sun early-employee role is near the age-26 boundary without a clear dated ≤26 founding or product milestone of the type this rubric requires for eligibility.
